chunks: 3157 - Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ḥujr al-Aslamī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

"Whoever comes to Mecca as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Medina, I will shun him on the Day of Judgment. And whoever comes to me as a visitor, my intercession becomes obligatory for him. And whoever has my intercession made obligatory for him, Paradise becomes obligatory for him. And whoever dies in one of the two sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina, will neither be presented nor reckoned, and he dies as one emigrating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and will be raised on the Day of Judgment with the companions of Badr."

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ بَدْرٍ: the companions who participated in the Battle of Badr
key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise as the promised final reward
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: the two sacred sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, the city of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.شَفَاعَتِي: the Prophet’s intercession on behalf of believers
key_terms.مُهَاجِراً: as one emigrating for the sake of Allah
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment and resurrection

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about visiting the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله after hajj and dying in Mecca or Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the merit of visiting the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله after performing hajj and highlights the spiritual rank of dying in Mecca or Medina. It connects ziyārah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله with shafa'ah, jannah, and a privileged state in the afterlife on the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3157 - It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from Ibrahim ibn Abi Hujr al-Aslami from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) stated:

"Whoever comes to Mecca for Hajj and does not visit me in Medina, I will show him indifference on the Day of Judgment. And whoever visits me as a pilgrim, my intercession will be guaranteed for him. And whoever is guaranteed my intercession is guaranteed Paradise. Whoever dies in one of the two sanctuaries, Mecca or Medina, will not be subjected to the presentation or accounting and will die as a migrant to Allah (swt), the Almighty, and will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment with the people of Badr."
